text:
Chicago's winless run reached five games (0-4-1) on a night when Ilya Mikheyev, a player who was never drafted and earned his way to the NHL as a free agent, scored twice for Tampa Bay in a 4-1 win. His second goal, a tip-in early in the third period, was the one that put the game away at 4-0.

The scoreboard made this look lopsided, but the play was closer than that. Our numbers put expected goals (the quality of chances each side created) at 2.82 for TBL and 1.95 for CHI, and the Lightning's simulated win share, how often they'd win if every shot were replayed, was 66 percent. At even strength the gap shrank to 2.05 to 1.90. Mikheyev's first goal in the opening period came on a 2 percent chance, and Ryan McDonagh's slap shot early in the third was also a 2 percent look. Victor Hedman had opened the scoring on the power play.

Andrei Vasilevskiy turned aside 25 of 26 shots, saving about one goal more than the chances against him suggested. Arvid Soderblom let in about 1.2 goals more than his 35 shots deserved, and that difference is where the margin came from. Roman Kantserov's tip-in with under a minute left spoiled the shutout. Chicago is now winless in five, while Tampa Bay takes the win and the two points.
